o: Count occurrences of each digit in the decimal representation of n and return the digit with the smallest count, breaking ties by the smaller digit. For 1553322 the digit 1 appears once; for 723344511 digits 7, 2, 5 each appear once and 2 is the smallest.
k: Simple frequency count over at most 10 digits.

a.i: Tally digits into a size-10 array, then scan digits 0..9 tracking the minimum (count, digit) lexicographically — scanning in ascending digit order automatically resolves ties toward the smaller digit.
s: Extract digits of n (handle n = 0 as a single 0 digit if relevant).
Scan d = 0..9 (present digits only) keeping the best (count, d).
a.t: O(log n) — number of digits, plus a constant 10-scan.

w: Scanning digits in ascending order makes tie-breaking automatic. Edge case: n = 0 (depending on constraints, n >= 1 here so it cannot occur, but defensive handling costs nothing). Follow-up: least frequent digit across a list of numbers, or k-least frequent.
